projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Richard Adams was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: This is Donna Steiger and I'm interviewing Richard Adams and this is March 10th, 2005, I forgot the date. And we are at the Armed Services Retirement Home.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Mr. Adams, can you tell me -- give me the date of your birth and where you were born?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: October the 4th, 1922 Paris, Texas.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And your father and mother, can you give me their names?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: My Dad is Ruben Alexander Adams and my Mothers name is Betty. His nickname was Rick. When he was a pitcher he used Rick?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you're saying he's a baseball player?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: He's a baseball player

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Can you give me an idea, a little bit about his background, a very short synopsis of it?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, he played -- I was born in '22 and he played ball in 1905 for Washington, he played for Washington and Philadelphia, and the Yankees one year. Then he went to Texas later.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you went to school then in Paris?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yes, my dad bought a farm in Paris, and he moved us all down there.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How many brothers and sisters did you have?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I have two brothers and one sister, and they're all deceased.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What -- tell me about -- did you finish school? Did you finish high school?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I didn't finish high school.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What grade did you go to?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was a junior when I joined the Navy.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How old were you?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was 19.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: 18 pardon me.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And that was in what year?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Were did you go to boot -- tell me a little bit about boot camp.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I -- well I went to boot camp in San Diego. Of course I served in the most unusual place in the world, real nice. It was a good _ of it. I went to radio school there.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And then when you got out -- how long was boot camp?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, boot camp was about let's see. I think about four weeks and then I went to radio school for about two more weeks.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you go to radio school in San Diego?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, San Diego.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Then what happened?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Then I went to Long Beach and caught the Phoenix, the S. S. Phoenix, Sail 46. And they took us to Pearl Harbor.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Were you the original crew on the Phoenix?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, I wasn't the original crew.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So take me on from Pearl Harbor.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Okay, we went to Pearl Harbor and we drove around there and drilled and stuff, getting under way from boot camp. We got to Hawaii in March 1941, training cruises and then they sent us on to world tour the Philippines. And we went to Cebu, Edoweebo(ph), and Vanbooden(ph) in the Philippines.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: All in the Philippines?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We stayed there a while and then we came back to Pearl again. It was kind of unusual; my Mother got a letter from me from the Philippines when Pearl Harbor was attacked. She said, "Oh, my son's safe. He's in Manila".

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And there you were in Hawaii?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was in Hawaii.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about the Pearl Harbor attack; tell me what you were doing.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well it was unusual. I just got off the mid- watch and they sent us all to General Porter. So I slowly put on my shoes and pants and went topside. Just as I stuck my head out the door, the Oklahoma turned over.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: You had heard the bombing? You heard the bombing or the planes or something?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I heard the shooting and the bombings and stuff. I still didn't realize what happened.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What did you think? Was just a drill?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was too -- I couldn't think. I just went on to battle station, you know, went to the emergency radio three decks below the water arm. I remember now I shouldn't have went down there. But I remember us getting under way.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about that how you got under way?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, when we first got under way there was about four or five of us.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Four or five ships?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Destroyers, couple of destroyers, couple of cruisers. We had a captain named Carmen Fisher, and the signal man told him, "Skipper, they're getting ready to close the sub-gate". He said, "Well tell them to go ahead and close it. I'll take it with me as I go out". He wanted to get out of there and I don't blame him. But we had seen the boys off the sunken ships on the beach waving at us and stuff covered with oil. Other than that it was exciting.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: You weren't frightened?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No I wasn't frightened. Too -- you know

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So there's about four or five of the ships took off then after the bombing?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah we went up and searched for them. Well, I got this message I was radioed, says get on the way immediately and engage the enemy 'cause that's what we tried to do but we couldn't find them.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you think there were submarines out there or what?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We knew there were submarines because one of them come in the harbor. And the destroyer, they already sunk one, I can't think of the name of the destroyer?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: The Arizona?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No it was a destroyer, that was a battle ship.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Small one.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: He sunk one, an unidentified submarine so he sunk it. Actually, it was the first shot of the war but we didn't know it at the time.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you went out to sea and then where did you head for or --

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We just went around looking for about two weeks.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: In the islands?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Around Honolulu, and then we came back in and then we started convoying civilians back to the states, two trips, and then they sent us to Sidney. And then from Sidney -- no, we went to Melvin first, then we went to Pearl _. There we -- what did we do there? Oh, and we picked up the U.S.S. Langley. That's an aircraft carrier. She was loaded with P-40 airplanes. And we were escorting her and we got a message from the Houston, a heavy cruiser. They wanted us to come help her. They were getting beat up pretty badly in the Java Sea, so we went to help them and told the Langley we were leaving we were going to help the Houston. And immediately after we left her they sunk the Langley.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh my goodness. How did you feel about that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, we thought that -- I didn't feel nothing then. She was on her way with those airplanes to the Netherlands, East Indies, and army of P-40's. We had to lose all those airplanes.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What about the people?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They got off.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: They got off?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah. Japanese aircraft destroyed -- didn't destroy them; hurt them enough where they had to abandon ship. But they had destroyers along with them and they picked up the crew and sank the Langley.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Meanwhile you're up at the Houston?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Then we went towards the Houston and the Java Sea, and we get about half way up to and they send us a message to get out of here, now. Then went back to _ Pearl, and stayed there for three months.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: 3 months?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And then we went to --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What were you doing there the three months?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We were just there, wasn't doing nothing. Then they sent us around to the western side of Australia, to the bridge vain (ph). Then we got ready for the Guadalcanal fight then.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Invasion?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Invasion and we protected them.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about that

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: That was -- well, we didn't do much. The Marines and the soldiers did all -- the Marines mainly.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: But you took them in there?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We took them in there and stood out there and watched.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How close did you get?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh, well we could see the Guadalcanal. We didn't get very close. And then we went to --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: You go in and pick them up any of them up then or what about the injured?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No we didn't go close to the beach at all. And then we -- what did we do then? Oh, after Guadalcanal, then they sent us to Philadelphia.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Like Philadelphia, Pennsylvania?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah to get an overhaul.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And we got there and we got overhauled, and we got radar and satellite, and then they sent us to Casablanca with Cordell Hull. I don't know why, they wouldn't tell us their secret

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So he was aboard your ship?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: He was aboard the ship; I guess he didn't like to fly on old aircraft. And we got back --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Was that pretty exciting to have him aboard?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh yeah, celebrity kind of, Secretary of State. And then we came back to Philadelphia and then they sent us back to SIG Fleet?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you -- when you came back from Casablanca was he coming back with you or he was over there?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No he came back with us. They didn't let us know too much, some kind of secret.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: But there must have been a lot of scuttle bug?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: It was 1943 so we didn't really know then. Now, we brought him home they sent us back to the SIG Fleet we went into the Seventh Fleet.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That was under Nimitz? Or who was that under?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We were MacArthur's Navy.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: MacArthur, okay?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: That's what they called us MacArthur's Navy, he was a soldier.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Who was your admiral though, was it Nimitz or something?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, I was on the staff of Admiral Cooper. He was aboard the Phoenix. We worked with the admiral and a couple of Australian Navy cruisers, HMAS, Australia.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So where did you pick up -- where did you pick up the Seventh fleet? Where were you when you picked them up?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I think we made an invasion in Cape Gloucester, in New Guinea.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Again carrying the Marines in or what, equipment?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We had some Army soldiers with us that time I think. Mostly we had Marines. Then we went to New Guinea. That's where I learned now to cook an Emu. Do you know what an Emu is?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Yes I do.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And they eat them. They said you take a big pot of boiling water, put the Emu in there, put a huge rock in there, when the rock gets soft its done. (Laughter)

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you were the radio man on board the Phoenix then -- so you're in New Guinea? That's a pretty wild country down there.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Hey, they're head hunters and cannibals.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Right

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And they don't like white people. They're too salty, or that's what they told me. I didn't want to find out.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So then where did you go after that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Then we started making all these little bombardments and landings, we would land soldiers and Marines and stuff.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Kind of tell us what that is since we can't read it.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: It's a --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: No just tell us where some of the places are?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: The landing was Cape Gloucester, Madang Bombardment, Los Negros landing, Seeadler Harbor, Hollandia landing, Biak, aircraft action off of Biak, and then we went to the biggest battle we had was the Surigao Strait battle.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Where is that located?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: That's in Leyte Gulf. That's where we got -- almost got hit by a suicide plane.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell us about that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Matter of fact, I was the flight radio which is three decks above the bridge on the bridge, and I'm watching them shoot at this plane coming in. We were under attack. Other than that I had no signal, I had my headphones on. Wasn't a signal coming so I'm watching him. And he was about 150 yards out when I fired these 25 shell heeds (ph) right in the middle. And I just think how stupid I was for standing there. He was coming right at me.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So he was headed for the ship, right?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: He was headed for the supper structure.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Was that the biggest battle you were in?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, well the Surigao Straights battle was the biggest one, besides Pearl Harbor --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: The Japanese was sending a fleet up from Singapore. We just landed at Leyte, we took MacArther into shore, he waded to shore in Leyte. But we knew they were coming because he had our PV wires out and they saw him coming. So we what they call crossing the T. We were -- we had all the old battle ships right here.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Uh, huh.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We were in front of them the cruisers, none of the destroyers were on their side, and we were circling and they were coming straight at us.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And that's what you call cross the T and they haven't got a chance, we wore them out and we won.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How many ships?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: There was a hundred ships that time.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How many did the United States lose then, anybody?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We didn't lose any; we just sunk all of theirs.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: We just sank all of theirs, and how many do you think they had?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They had -- we sunk one battle ship.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well we didn't sink it, we hit her first. The _ 'cause you had them zeroed in.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That's right.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They were sitting there waiting for us.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That's right. Were there prisoners off of that, did you get prisoners off of that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No we got one prisoner I think one time. They didn't like to be captured.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Yeah, I know that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And then --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So then where -- tell me more about some of your battle trips.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Okay, well after Surigao Straights and then I told you about the aircraft action.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh, and then when we took Manila in the Philippines we went up to Corregidor.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh, wow.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And there were still Japanese on the Corregidor.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: So we bombed them every morning to start the battle.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Kind of get them softened up right?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: For three days.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And then --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: We lost a lot of boys on Corredidor.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Was that Marines or Army?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They were Army.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Army.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They had death marked the head of the baton.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Yeah, I remember that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I still got my coal.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Okay. So anyway, you were softening up Corregador for the invasion?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, well when we got through they surrendered.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How long that take?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Took about a week.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: A week?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We went over and they let us have liberty in Manila, and we'd go by one of these big banks and there was money laying all over the street and wasn't any good, pesos, that blew up. And then what happened? I think we were --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So after Corregidor so where were you on VJ Day?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was in Treasure Island waiting for a ship.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Well, let's take you from Corregador and get you back to Treasure Island here. How did --

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Right after -- right after we finished with the Philippines, they transferred me to _. And I was back in TI _ was a war zone waiting for the U.S.S. Pergy (ph) 741. I think I have got it, yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What rate were you then, were you a T?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was a T-6 First Class.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: First Class Radio One?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I made Chief a little later.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So VJ day was there and were you on Market Street on VJ Day?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They wouldn't let us ashore.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That's too bad.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They wouldn't let me go ashore because I was getting transferred the next morning.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Too bad, I was there.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And they sent us to Tokyo.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh wow.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We were part of the invasion force.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you -- tell me about how you got your ship then first. And then you what -- was that out of Honolulu that they went on to Tokyo or what?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, after the war was over, I was in San Francisco, I got aboard that destroyer.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And they sent me to Tokyo.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Directly?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: No stopping?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, we didn't even stop in Honolulu

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How many ships went over there to Tokyo?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Just a couple because we didn't need any then they had already surrendered.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you were with the first group into Tokyo?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well no, MacArthur was there. He took the ceremony aboard the ship, and --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Right I remember that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And then we went in and then we came back to Long Beach I think. Then they put me on a strange one, Mount McKinley.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Can we go back to Tokyo? Did you get liberty at Tokyo?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, I got liberty.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me what you thought about that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: It was kind of scary 'cause you're over there by yourself with people you just been fighting. Make you nervous. You know, somebody might have a grudge or get killed or something.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Were they friendly at all?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, they were friendly, real friendly. Bought a bunch of souvenirs and stuff.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you were more frightened than they were? A Yeah, well I was just uncomfortable, put it that way 'cause you're over there with people that you just been fighting and they surrendered. Some of them might not give up yet, one or two of then you know. I had to get back home and drink some more tea.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: All right, so then you came back to -- after Tokyo you came back to --

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Long Beach.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Long Beach?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And went aboard the communicating ship, Mount McKinley. And then we went and shot the bombs, Operation Cross roads.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about that, I don't know about that.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, you probably seen it on TV. Had the bikini --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: The island?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: The island, the little island.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: We were testing bombs?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Testing the atomic bomb.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What did you do down there?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We had a 150 radio men on one watch, on the Mount Mckinley. We sent a lot of traffic.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Lot of traffic out?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Out. They let us go over and watch them.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What did you think about that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well I felt -- I don't know what it was. I didn't like them letting us do that. But I just sit there and watch. I had goggles on, dark glasses and watch the explosion of the under water ones, and see this wave coming right at you.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That's scary.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: It is. You're not supposed to do that I don't think.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you had the under water not the --

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We didn't have the aerial.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: -- aerial. So it was a ship --

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: The shock wave you could see it.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And it -- when it hit the ship?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, we weren't' that far off.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Wow. And how long were you out there?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Just as long enough for them to - operation to test.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Then you left there you're still on board the same ship?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No I wasn't. I was long gone from the Phoenix.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: I know, but the other ship you were on?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Mount McKinley?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Uh, huh.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: They took those back to the states and sent me where? Oh, I do put the U.S.S. DuPont in commission.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Where about was that?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: That's in Newport, Rhode Island.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you came back in to Long Beach and then they flew you to Rhode Island or you went by ship?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: To the canal?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No I was -- where did I get orders? I thought I got orders from California to go to Newport to put the ship in commission. By the time they -- well, before I did that though I had shore duty in New York City, 90 church street I was one of the instructors there of the reserve.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you were training?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: We were training reserves in Brooklyn, New York; all this was on at 90 Church Street. And after I did three years there I was married by then, had two children.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Where was your wife living?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: She lived in Paris. She stayed there while I was putting the ship in commission. They did get to go with me when I went to Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Tell me about -- take me, now you're in New York training and then you went to Newport Beach?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, I went to actually, New York, I went to Greenland.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: On the ship?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: No, no on shore duty.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Uh, huh.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And it was kind of a deal. You volunteer for it you get 30 days leave 'cause you do nine months up there, they give you 30 days leave and it didn't count on your record so I volunteered. And then after that I went to --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What did you do up there?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Sent radio weather messages. ____ Green lines it's called.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So then when did you get married?

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: You were still playing around the Pacific?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, I was still in the Pacific then.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: You married a girl from your home town?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And you have two children, a boy and a girl?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah two children, a boy and a girl

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So what's this Guantanamo, when did you go to Cuba?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well after I come back from Greenland, after I went to -- Castro was still -- he wasn't there yet when I went.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Batista.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Batista was the boss because when he finished our tour in Guantanamo bay, I drove back. I had a car down there, drove to Key West, no to Havana. Took the ferry across to Key West, and drove all the way up the coast to California.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: How long were you in Guantanamo?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Three years.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Did you enjoy it?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh yeah. I got _____.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh my goodness.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: That was good duty, huh?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: That was good duty.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So then you came back into Key West, came across the United States to California, then what happened?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Then I went to Norfolk, Virginia then. Got aboard the Alocane (ph) AKA 55 and that's when we went to Mezrani, Naples, Cedar Bay Creek, French Riviera, Beirut Lebanon, wasn't like it is now.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you were aboard this one ship for all this time?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Then I got shore duty in __that's another Navy reserve training center. I was the chief in charge of _ on that one.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Is that where you retired from?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was getting close to retirement. Then I went to _ maintenance school in _. And then went on a boy's ship and then retired.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What ship did you go aboard, the last one?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: David, another destroyer. And then --

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: What's the most of the exciting thing that happened of all -- if you had to pick one of the exciting things of the years that you spent in the Navy, what would be the most exciting thing?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Well, probably Pearl Harbor.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Pearl Harbor?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yes it was exciting.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Also the scariest?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Scariest and the Surigao Straights.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So when did you retire?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: '61, and went back to Paris. And then got a job in Lovit(ph), Texas and went up there.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: When do you do in Lovit(ph)?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was a post man.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh my goodness.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I did 20 years in the post office.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Is that right in Lovit(ph), Texas?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So how did you come -- how did you arrive here at the home?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: My wife passed away and I couldn't stand to be by myself anymore. After 56 years, you get kind of used to people.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Where are your children?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Ones in Austin, and the other ones in Lovitt. The daughter came here to see me the other Christmas, and she got caught in the snow. They drove up.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh my goodness.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: But they enjoy it, took them five days to drive up here.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you have really enjoyed the Navy life?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh yeah.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Sounds like you've seen a lot of the world.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I've been everywhere.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Which would be your favorite place? Not the most exciting, we talked about that but your favorite?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Oh, that was in Chili in South America. The reason it's my favorite place is because you get 750 sols for $1.00.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Oh that's why you liked it.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: And you could buy a can of beer for 30 sols.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: My goodness.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: For 750 of them you give them $1.00. We were thinking about moving down there and retiring.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So you've been at the home here for how long?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: For about a year, a little over a year about two months, December.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: And you enjoy it?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: Yeah, I had a bad cold I couldn't get rid of it.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Okay that's good. What else would you like to tell your family? This is your story.

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I guess I told them all I need to tell them, all they want to hear from me.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: So when you retired you were what? What was your rate or rank?

sp.speaker: Richard Adams
sp.p: I was Chief Radio _ engine.

sp.speaker: Donna Steiger
sp.p: Okay that's good. Well, it's been a good interview, that's good. I'm glad you really enjoyed the Navy and you had such a lustrous career, two careers actually.
